title: Program Anatomy: An ELF Reader From Scratch

questions.question: Which rule applies to every analysis target in lessons 32 to 36?
options: The target is a program you wrote and compiled yourself
The target is a program with a published source map
The target is a program smaller than one megabyte
The target is any program installed on your machine
questions.explanation: The track analyzes only code you own. That keeps every lesson inside the authorization rules of 17 U.S.C. 1201(f), Directive 2009/24/EC, Sega, and Connectix.

questions.question: A symbol in a relocatable object has st_value 0x10 and st_shndx 2, and section 2 has sh_offset 0x40 and sh_addr 0. Where are its bytes in the file?
options: At file offset 0x50, the section offset plus the value
At file offset 0x42, the section index plus the value
At file offset 0x10, because st_value is a file offset
At file offset 0x40, the start of its section
questions.explanation: In an object st_value is an offset inside the symbol's section. The file offset is sh_offset + st_value - sh_addr, here 0x40 + 0x10 - 0 = 0x50.

questions.question: A record in .rela.text reads offset 0x36, R_X86_64_PC32, .rodata+0x10, and the lea instruction that holds the field ends at 0x3a. Where does the lea point after linking?
options: At .rodata+0x36, the offset of the field
At .rodata+0x10, the addend names the target
At .text+0x10, relocations always point into the patched section
At .rodata+0x14, since S + A - P is added to the end of the instruction
questions.explanation: The processor adds the stored value to 0x3a. The stored value is S + A - P with P = 0x36, so the result is .rodata + 0x10 + 4 = .rodata + 0x14.

questions.question: Which structure does the ELF loader read to map an executable into memory?
options: The string table, found through e_shstrndx
The program header table, found through e_phoff
The symbol table, found through .symtab
The section header table, found through e_shoff
questions.explanation: Program headers are the execution view. A stripped executable can have no section header table at all and still run.

questions.question: How does a Mach-O reader find the length of a function from an nlist_64 entry?
options: It reads the n_desc field, which stores the function size in bytes
It takes the next symbol address in the same section minus this one
It reads the size from the section_64 record that contains the symbol
It reads the size from the LC_SYMTAB command, one field per symbol
questions.explanation: nlist_64 has n_strx, n_type, n_sect, n_desc, and n_value, and no size field. The ELF st_size has no Mach-O counterpart in an object file.

questions.question: Why do the lesson tests compare the reader with captured llvm-objdump text instead of running the tool?
options: Because captured text parses faster than running the tool in each test
Because llvm-objdump cannot read relocatable objects without a Linux sysroot
Because the comparison runs on any machine and the oracle cannot drift
Because the course forbids every external tool, including the compiler
questions.explanation: The fixture holds the tool output from one known tool version. The tests need no tool installed, and a later tool release cannot change what the reader is compared against.
